title: A/B rollout harness for adaptive batching & KV-prefix caching config experiments
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: We have several heuristic recommendations in Redwood Optimize that suggest batching and KV-prefix caching profiles per workload. Customers have different latency/cost trade-offs and historically we lack an automated, safe way to validate cost savings without regressions in latency or quality. Goal: Build an A/B experimentation harness and dashboards to validate automated batching + prefix-caching recommendations, enable gradual traffic rollouts, and implement reliable apply/rollback triggers.

Hypothesis: Applying the recommended batching + KV-prefix caching profile will reduce token-level cost by >= 15% on read-heavy request patterns while keeping p95 latency increase <= 10ms and model quality regressions < 0.5% (measured by eval prompt set).

Key metrics to capture (observability + analysis):
- cost_per_1M_tokens: cost estimate derived from GPU-seconds and resources used
- p50/p95/p99_inference_latency_ms: end-to-end service latency measured at request boundary
- effective_throughput_tps: tokens/sec per model pool
- avg_batch_size and batch_size_distribution: histogram of batch sizes
- kv_cache_hit_rate: percent requests that hit prefix cache
- quality_regression_rate: fraction of failed/low-quality outputs flagged by eval probes and automated LLM-eval checks
- error_rate and 5xx_rate: service-level errors
- rollback_triggers_fired: boolean flag per experiment window

Instrumentation plan: add experiment tags to request traces (experiment_id, cohort=A/B, config_version). Emit batch-level metrics from runtime (batch size histograms) and cache metrics from KV service. Add sampling of decoded outputs for automatic eval (rate-limited). Create a temporary per-experiment cost model that maps GPU utilization to estimated $/token.

Experiment design: 
- Unit of randomization: route + api_key (so repeated users stick to cohort)
- Sample size: target at least 100k requests per cohort for statistically powered detection of 10% cost change at alpha=0.05 (see sample size calc in Confluence link).
- Traffic split: 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% with 12h minimum observation window at each step and automated health checks before progress.
- Statistical tests: for cost and latency use bootstrap CI on medians and difference-in-differences; for quality use proportion tests (two-proportion z-test) and A/B buckets for noisy labels.

Safe apply/rollback controls: feature-flagged config apply with versioned config objects, canary cohorts, circuit-breaker that will auto-rollback on any of: p95 latency delta > 50ms, error_rate increase > 0.5pp, cost savings negative beyond 5% and quality_regression_rate > 1%. All auto-rollbacks are recorded and annotated with root-cause signals and linked to the incident runbook.

Dashboards and reports: new A/B experiment dashboard per-experiment showing live cohorts, cohort-level metrics, rolling-window deltas, CI bands, and automated recommendations summary. A daily digest report will summarize experiment outcome, resource savings estimate, and suggested next action (promote, tune, or abort).

Acceptance criteria and deliverables: see acceptance_criteria field.

Notes: This ticket focuses on the experimentation harness, metrics, dashboards, and rollback automation. Tuning of recommendation engine (model that suggests the profiles) is tracked in ENG-4055.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Experiment framework can create and manage an experiment with a unique ID and two cohorts (control & candidate) for a given route and api_key segment.
2) Runtime emits cohort-tagged metrics: batch_size histogram, kv_cache_hit_rate, per-request latency, and resource usage.
3) A/B dashboard exists with cohort overlays, delta windows, CI bands, and a clear promote/rollback button.
4) Gradual rollout orchestration is implemented (1% -> 5% -> 25% -> etc) with automated health checks and the ability to pause/rollback.
5) Auto-rollback triggers are configurable and were exercised in a staged canary test (recorded in comments).
6) A short Postmortem template and experiment summary is auto-generated after experiment end.
7) Documentation (Confluence) and a README for on-call are published and linked.
